name_reason: Compliant data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> name. Prefix data_fd2_ (game global), domain 'chapter' correct, 'ch20' is chapter ID 20 (range 01-30, meaningful, must keep), 'end_scene1' = chapter-20 END handler scene 1, 'char_pos_y_table' reflects the array/table data type and Y-coordinate semantics. No Ghidra address residue (no _52206/hex suffix); the only numerals (ch20, scene1) are meaningful domain IDs.
purpose: Const lookup table of scene-1 world Y positions for party slots 0..15 in the chapter-20 end cutscene.
logic_summary: 16-byte const byte table read only by fd2_chapter_20_end (@0x23E74). Prologue REP MOVSD-copies it from 0x52206 into stack scratch [ESP+0x10], then the slot-placement loop (i=0..15) writes runtime_char[i].bPos_y = table[i] while runtime_char[i].bPos_x comes from the sibling scene1_x table @0x521F6 and pSprite_state[1]=1. Values 0x21-0x25 are world-grid Y positions consistent with view-window/cursor origin Y=0x1F set by the same handler.
element_semantics: Each byte = world-grid Y coordinate (0x21..0x25) for the party member at slot index 0..15 in scene 1 of the chapter-20 end cutscene; copied verbatim into runtime_char[slot].bPos_y.
notes: Both xrefs to 0x52206 are READ/DATA only (0x23EA0 READ, 0x23E9B DATA) -> no game-side write -> const confirmed (src already declares const). Memory bytes at 0x52206 (23 24 22 22 23 24 21 22 23 24 25 21 22 23 24 25) match the src const initializer exactly. Source group-header comment (chend2.c lines 34-42) already accurately and tersely documents all four sibling tables incl. this y-table; kept unchanged. Ghidra data plate was <null>; created a concise PLATE_COMMENT (per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism: cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...) via run_script_inline). No src edit made (comment kept), so only the shard file is staged.
